chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
He should not shave his head nor visit (the shrine) until he offers the sacrifice, then he shall shave his head and visit whenever he wishes.
ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim shave their head during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the chronological precedence of the animal sacrifice (dhabh) over the shaving of the head (halq) and visiting the shrine (ziyarat) during Hajj. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the specific ritual order prescribed by the Imams, ensuring that the pilgrim completes the core act of sacrifice before engaging in the subsequent acts of purification and devotion.
